intro: What this realm relies on when it relies on somebody else's certificate. Every use case goes through one validation door; this page shows what that door holds each one to, the certificate authorities it may reach, and what is pinned.
paranoidNote: auto is on in product mode and off in development. While it is in force each use case below is held to the full checks; a use case switched off, or every use case while it is not in force, behaves as it did before paranoid PKI mode existed, and nothing else changes.
phase: enforced at its sites from rollout phase {phase}
signersNote: The certificate authorities, and the intermediates under them, a third party's certificate may chain to when it is relied on for anything but a TLS handshake. This list is this realm's own. A leaf never goes here: a leaf to pin goes on the entry or relationship that uses it.
fileSet: {file} gave {n} of the entries below (pki.signerTrustAnchorsFile, default realm only).
emptySigners: This realm's signer truststore is empty.
addNote: Paste one or more PEM certificates. A self-signed CA becomes an anchor and any other CA an intermediate, which must chain to an anchor held. Each refusal is named.
addPurposes: Trust them only for these use cases (none ticked means every use case):
addAccept: Accept this one server certificate by name, for outbound TLS only. It is still held to its validity and fields, and to any revocation list it names.
pinsNote: Every certificate this realm relies on because somebody registered it, held to the checks whatever the settings above say. Last audited: {when}.
emptyPins: Nothing pinned has been audited in this realm.
clientNote: A different store: the {n} anchor(s) a TLS client certificate is verified against at a handshake. It is the process's, not this realm's, because a handshake has no realm in it.
truststoresNote: Every truststore this realm can name. Each use case trusts the truststores it is assigned on the Use cases tab, or its default list. A named truststore is kept in the directory; one created in the default realm is service-wide and any realm may name it.
notInstalled: The directory that keeps named truststores is not installed in this process, so none can be created or assigned here.
whereBuiltIn: Shipped with this service or derived from it; it cannot be changed.
whereSigners: Changed on the Signer truststore tab.
whereSpiffe: Changed by SPIFFE federation, where its bundle is kept.
whereShared: Service-wide: changed from the default realm.
createNote: A name is 1 to 63 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, and none of the built-in names. A truststore created in the default realm is service-wide; one created in any other realm serves that realm only. A realm holds at most {max}. Each certificate added is a CA: a self-signed one is an anchor, any other an intermediate that must chain to an anchor held, and a leaf is refused.
useCasesNote: Every place this service validates a certificate or dials a TLS server, and the truststores it trusts, in order, in every mode. Paranoid PKI mode decides what is checked on the path, never which truststores are consulted. A service-wide use case has no realm in hand, so it names only the default realm's truststores and is assigned from the default realm.
assignHint: Truststores, in order, separated by commas
notAssignablePins: Trusts the certificate registered on each entry; nothing to assign.
notAssignableFixed: This service's own hierarchy by definition; not assigned.
notAssignableAdmission: An admission rule, not a trust decision; not assigned.
assignedFromDefault: Service-wide: assigned from the default realm.
systemNote: Node's default store, which the built-in truststore system holds: the root certificates bundled with node (Mozilla's list) plus any in NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS. It is changed by rebuilding the image or by setting that variable, not here.
